summary: Heaven & Ale has you moving a shared rondel-like track to gather ingredients and monks while carefully layering colored barrel tiles to maximize scoring runs. It's a tight, efficient engine game where spatial puzzle-solving on your barrel board matters as much as resource collection.
praised: elegant tension between garden expansion and harvesting
criticised: rondel/turn-order mechanism can feel fiddly at first
barrel scoring math takes a game or two to click
limited direct player interaction beyond spot competition

interaction.detail: Players race for shared spaces on a central rondel and monk track, occasionally blocking each other from ideal actions, but nearly all scoring happens on each player's own barrel board independent of others.

scoring.why: Each barrel row scores only as far as its shortest completed row reaches, so your weakest ingredient track caps your points regardless of how far the others advanced.
scoring.how_you_win: Expand your garden and harvest grain, hops, fruit, and water in balance, then place them into barrel rows; because scoring is capped by your shortest row, the player who keeps all resource tracks evenly developed (plus refinement bonuses) scores highest.
